messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed from us-east2 egress cluster (primary). 5xx rate spiked to ~18% over the last 5m. Linked alert: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/AE-5482

maya (oncall): acked. I'm looking at the serving nodes in us-east2 now. pulling recent logs and egress metrics.

ow: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l egress=us-east2 -o wide`

ow: checking egress gateway health and BGP sessions.

ow: I see elevated connection resets on gw-us-east2-a and high queue drops on the primary egress fabric.

ow: tagging pagerduty: @pagerduty — we'll be paging neteng.

ow: paging owen (neteng): @owen can you take a look at egress GW health? suspecting ACL or upstream peer flapping.

owen (neteng): on it. I can see upstream peer sending RSTs and some mismatch in MTU shaping after the 03:06 deploy. Pulling tcpdumps now.

ow: quick mitigations: two options — (1) shift outgoing routed traffic for hosted API to us-east2-b (secondary egress) with traffic-shift script (fast), or (2) attempt ACL rollback on gw-us-east2-a (risky if the bad ACL touched many peers). Recommend (1) to reduce customer impact immediately.

maya (oncall): agree. Initiating targeted traffic shift for customer-facing production routes first (non-Dedicated). Will keep Dedicated and Private traffic pinned until we confirm stability.

maya (oncall): running traffic shift:```sh
# traffic-shift to secondary egress (safe, gradual)
./tools/egress-shift --from=us-east2-a --to=us-east2-b --service=api --percent=30
```

maya (oncall): initiated 30% shift. Observing metrics.

10m later

maya (oncall): metrics update — 5xx rate is down to ~9% overall; partial improvement. Increasing shift to 70% now.```sh
./tools/egress-shift --from=us-east2-a --to=us-east2-b --service=api --percent=70
```

ow: alert: incident-bot auto-post: Pager duty escalation threshold hit — paging L2 neteng.

ow: support-lead: drafting external status page and customer comms now. Posting draft here for review.

support-lead: STATUS PAGE DRAFT (public):
We are currently investigating increased error rates affecting requests routed through our US-East region (us-east2). We have identified a networking issue impacting the primary egress gateway and are rerouting traffic to a secondary egress to reduce impact. Customers may see increased latency or transient errors. We will post another update within 30 minutes.

support-lead: CUSTOMER NOTIFICATION (Dedicated / SLA customers):
Hi <CustomerName>,
We’re investigating elevated error rates in our US‑East (us-east2) egress. We have rerouted traffic to a secondary egress node to mitigate impact. There is no indication of data loss, and we’ll provide updates every 30 minutes until fully resolved. If you rely on pinned egress routes for compliance, we can coordinate a temporary change.

jordan (solutions): For Private/VPC customers that need immediate reroute guidance: share these IPs and DNS endpoints — `egress-b.us-east2.redwood.net` (secondary) and `egress-c.us-east2.redwood.net` (fallback). Recommend updating customer CNAMEs or firewall allowlist to include those immediately while we resolve.

ow: owen (neteng): we've shifted 100% of non-Dedicated production traffic to us-east2-b. Primary still showing packet drops when we try to send, so leaving Dedicated pinned. Investigating a faulty ACL pushed by automation during the 03:06 deploy; it appears a rule blocked established connections to an upstream transit peer.

now: maya (oncall): comms: posting the status page now. Also sending the Dedicated customer list to support (DM). support-lead confirm you have list?

support-lead: got it, sending targeted emails now with the Dedicated template. Also posting the public status update.

now: owen (neteng): rolling back the recent ACL change on gw-us-east2-a to test if that resolves peer resets. Command:```sh
ssh gw-us-east2-a
sudo iptables-restore < /etc/fw/backup/2026-03-XX/fw-predeploy.rules
```

now: owen (neteng): rollback applied to gw-us-east2-a. Monitoring for peer stabilization.

10m later

ow: monitoring: primary egress packet drop decreased to near baseline, 5xx rate across region now ~0.6%. Good signal.

ow: maya (oncall): great. We'll keep traffic on secondary for an additional 15 minutes while we validate end-to-end. After validation, we'll move traffic back to primary gradually.

now: emily (oncall-next): taking over watch in 30m. please add runbook and summary for handoff.

maya (oncall): handoff summary (add to channel and oncall doc):
- incident start: 1750001234 (~03:06 deploy)
- impact: elevated 5xx affecting hosted API in us-east2; Dedicated customers unaffected (pinned)
- mitigation taken: gradual traffic shift to us-east2-b; rollback of recent ACL on gw-us-east2-a
- current status: primary shows baseline, 100% non-Dedicated traffic on secondary with confirmation that primary restored; waiting 15m observation window
- action items: verify long-term fix for automation ACL deployment, add pre-deploy check to prevent ACL regressions, notify Dedicated customers about temporary reroute availability if needed

maya (oncall): EMILY — please own the post-resolution verification (logs, BGP stability, and alert suppression) and coordinate RCA with NetEng and Deploy teams. I'll leave notes in the incident doc.

emily (oncall-next): acknowledged. I'll be on watch and will escalate if anything regresses.

now: 45m after start

incident-bot: Incident status: RESOLVED :white_check_mark:
Root cause: an automated firewall/ACL change pushed during a routine deploy blocked established sessions to an upstream transit peer, causing packet drops and connection resets on the primary egress gateway.
Resolution actions: rolled back the ACL change on gw-us-east2-a; shifted traffic to us-east2-b during mitigation; added a preflight check in the deploy pipeline to validate ACLs before pushing.

incident-bot: Postmortem link: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/AE-5482-postmortem

maya (oncall): closing thread — will update the public status page to RESOLVED and send the RCA to customers within the hour. Thanks @owen and @support-lead for quick work.

support-lead: scheduling outbound RCA emails to affected customers and Dedicated contacts. template and list attached to the incident doc.

jordan (solutions): noted for Private customers — we'll push a follow-up note with recommended DNS/allowlist changes and timeline for a permanent fix.

pagerduty: Incident AE-5482 marked resolved by maya.
